requirements.requirement: node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2
requirements.summary: dnsmasq was installed and configured on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.174.11, started and enabled. dig against both 127.0.0.1 and node1's IP returned 10.100.174.11, and upstream names (www.redhat.com) still resolved via forwarding, confirming both the specific mapping and general resolver function.

requirements.requirement: node2 is configured to use node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups
requirements.summary: NetworkManager's eth0 profile on node2 was set with ipv4.dns=10.100.174.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes, persisted in the connection profile, /etc/resolv.conf reflected nameserver 10.100.174.10, and dig/getent resolved inventory-api.internal to 10.100.174.11 while upstream lookups still worked through node1.

requirements.requirement: node1 survives restart with resolver service and mapping intact (provider-wide restart evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 809708f3... and healthy dnsmasq captured before restart; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); a new boot_id 25c1af7f... observed after polling; post-restart checks show dnsmasq active/enabled, firewalld dns service persisted, and dig confirms inventory-api.internal still resolves to node2. Cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot, which matches the same new boot_id.

requirements.requirement: node2 survives restart with resolver configuration and resolution intact (provider-wide restart evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d72bd4ec... and healthy resolv.conf/resolution captured before restart; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 6cb40733... observed after polling; post-restart resolv.conf still points at node1, the NM profile retains ipv4.dns/ipv4.ignore-auto-dns, and dig/getent confirm inventory-api.internal still resolves correctly. Cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot, which matches.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: node1 runs dnsmasq resolving inventory-api.internal to node2's IP while forwarding other queries upstream, and node2's NetworkManager profile persistently points at node1 as its DNS resolver, verified end-to-end. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also executed correctly for both nodes, with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and confirmed recovery of dnsmasq, firewall rules, NM DNS settings, and resolution behavior. Hygiene is good; the only minor blemish is bind-utils being left installed on both nodes solely for verification tooling, which is low-risk and non-disruptive.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) at all three lifecycle snapshots, so native package-manager consistency after the temporary vault.centos.org repo usage could not be directly confirmed, though the repo files themselves were verified removed.

The node1 post-restart firewalld check without sudo failed with an authorization error (cmd-a912b2a03f2642d4); however, a follow-up sudo call (cmd-f63e96c2dc044577) confirmed the dns service was still present, so this is not treated as a failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were largely necessary and bounded. The temporary vault.centos.org repo files added to work around missing subscription-manager repos were removed immediately after each install (cmd-c0d5deaa454e42f4, cmd-b343385fc0e2429c, cmd-9b396af2ba3f4135), leaving no repo residue. The dnsmasq install/config and firewalld dns opening on node1 (cmd-c0d5deaa454e42f4, cmd-d12468a64e7f424c) and the nmcli DNS changes on node2 (cmd-9b396af2ba3f4135) are required, retained changes directly satisfying the task. A minor unnecessary retention: bind-utils was installed on both node1 (cmd-b343385fc0e2429c) and node2 (cmd-9b396af2ba3f4135) purely to obtain a dig/verification tool and was not removed afterward, leaving a small, low-risk package footprint not strictly required by the task contract, though reasonable for producing verification evidence. No failed services, conflicting units, or unsafe exposure were observed; failed-services lists remained empty in both before/after lifecycle snapshots. The two reboots (cmd-9e7734da37964d42, cmd-bf5a882a09cb483e) were bounded, expected under the restart-evidence protocol, and fully recovered.
